synopsis: Across Chapter 5 and the glossary, the four-month validation window makes tests per wall-clock hour more important than real-time rendering [f4350, f13559]. Headless simulation computes only required test quantities without pictures; object-list braking tests can represent the machine and worker as points and calculate stopping distance [f13555, f13556]. These runs use ordinary processors, run far faster than real time, and can scale across thousands of cheap processor cores, supporting the recommendation to run most of the millions of braking-logic combinations headless [f13557, f13561]. Rendering is needed when camera, lidar or radar models require scene views, but GPU ray tracing slows simulation toward real time or below [f13558]. The recommended allocation is therefore broad screening with lower-fidelity models and scarce high-fidelity rendered runs for perception-sensitive cases selected through correlation and sensitivity work; the facts provide no numerical split between these workloads [f13560, f13562].
